c.tagline: Danube river town crowned by the world's tallest church spire

taxi.fareNote: Standard German metered taxis; ranks at the Hauptbahnhof and Münsterplatz, or booked by phone/app

emergency.note: Fast, reliable emergency response; English-speaking operators are common

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Fischerviertel: Half-timbered houses on the Blau canals

hood_desc: Ulm's compact medieval core, dominated by the 161.5-meter spire of Ulm Minster, the tallest church tower on Earth. Cobblestone squares, the ornate town hall, and Einstein's birthplace memorial all sit within a few minutes' walk of each other. It's the obvious first stop and stays lively with cafes and shops.

The Fishermen's and Tanners' Quarter, a picture-postcard tangle of half-timbered houses along the little Blau River canals just south of the Altstadt. Leaning, centuries-old buildings house restaurants and boutique hotels, making it one of the most photographed corners of southern Germany.

A mixed residential and nightlife district along the Danube promenade, popular with students and young professionals for its bars, riverside bike paths, and contemporary art spaces like the Kunsthalle Weishaupt. It feels more relaxed and less touristy than the old town.

A quiet, leafy district built around a former Poor Clares monastery, Söflingen Abbey, now offering a calmer, residential alternative to central Ulm. Local bakeries and small parks give it a village-like feel despite being minutes from downtown.

A hillside district anchored by the University of Ulm and its associated science park, with sweeping views back over the city and the Danube valley. It's quiet and largely residential, popular with students and academics rather than tourists.

water.note: German tap water is safe and strictly regulated.

train: Ulm Hauptbahnhof sits on the ICE high-speed line between Stuttgart and Munich, roughly 40 min and 1 hr away respectively
bus: FlixBus and regional buses connect Ulm to nearby cities and the airports

car.idp: Not required for EU/UK/US short stays

tip.r: Round the bill up or add roughly 5-10% at restaurants; tell the server the total including tip rather than leaving cash on the table

landmarks: Ulm Minster (Ulmer Münster)
The world's tallest church spire soars 161 metres above the Danube; climb its 768 steps for views stretching to the Alps on clear days.
Fishermen's Quarter (Fischerviertel)
A storybook maze of half-timbered houses, footbridges and mill wheels along the little Blau river, once home to Ulm's fishermen and tanners.
Ulm Town Hall (Rathaus)
A flamboyantly frescoed Gothic-Renaissance hall adorned with an ornate astronomical clock and a replica of Berblinger's famous flying machine inside.
Schiefes Haus (Crooked House)
A 14th-century half-timbered house leaning improbably over the Blau, celebrated by Guinness as the world's most crooked hotel and endlessly photographed.
Metzgerturm (Butchers' Tower)
Ulm's own leaning tower, a 14th-century city gate tilting two metres off vertical, guarding the walkable medieval walls along the Danube.
Wiblingen Monastery Library
A short ride south, this former Benedictine abbey conceals one of Germany's most dazzling Rococo library halls, all gilded columns and swirling ceiling frescoes.
Museum Ulm
Home of the 40,000-year-old Lion Man (Löwenmensch), the world's oldest known figurative sculpture, alongside strong medieval and modern art collections.
Einstein Fountain and Memorial
Jürgen Goertz's whimsical bronze fountain of a rocket-snail with Einstein's face honours the physicist near his 1879 birthplace site in his native city.
Danube Riverside Walk and City Wall
A leafy promenade atop the old fortifications where you can stroll between towers, watch river barges and gaze across the Danube into Bavaria.
Kunsthalle Weishaupt
A glass-fronted contemporary gallery on the Neue Mitte square, showing pop art and post-war abstraction from Warhol to Josef Albers from a private collection.

train.note: Ulm Hbf is on the main Stuttgart-Munich line, and the new high-speed section opened in 2022 cut Stuttgart to about 30 minutes; Munich takes just over an hour. EuroCity trains to Zurich and Railjets toward Vienna pass through, giving the city direct international links despite its size. DB Sparpreis fares open six months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches stop at the Hauptbahnhof forecourt. FlixBus runs to Munich, Stuttgart and onward into Austria and Switzerland, though the train is faster on the main corridors. Carry your passport or EU ID card for cross-border services.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled ferry. Ulm sits on the upper Danube, which is not navigable for passenger services this far upstream - the traditional Ulmer Schachtel boats are a summer novelty ride.

half.name: Blaubeuren
half.blurb: Blaubeuren has the Blautopf, a strikingly blue karst spring pool, next to a former Benedictine monastery.

half.name: Augsburg
half.blurb: Augsburg is one of Germany's oldest cities, with a Renaissance city hall and the Fuggerei, the world's oldest social housing complex.

half.name: Legoland Germany
half.blurb: Legoland Germany in Gunzburg is a theme park built around Lego bricks, with rides for families.

half.name: Bad Urach
half.blurb: Bad Urach is a half-timbered spa town below a ruined hilltop castle, with a waterfall dropping through a wooded gorge.
